display.purpose: Page H1s on the field. Tool and error heroes 2.875rem on phones, 3.75rem from 640px; 3.75rem / 4.25rem (1440px+) in the desktop hero seam. The full ramp is the blog index title.

headline.purpose: Section H2s on the counter, always under a 2px ink counter rule.

title.purpose: Card titles, FAQ summaries, step titles in bold system sans.

body.purpose: Ledes and paragraphs; FAQ answers capped at 68ch.

label.purpose: Ticket header strip, hero aside column labels, footer column labels, table heads.

serial.purpose: Real pin-ID serial in the ticket header, repeated on the receipt band; article serial strip and article-ticket stubs.

stub.purpose: The tear-off Download stub and the receipt's collect button.

article-title.purpose: One per blog article, on the field; sized against the masthead text column (container units).

article-section.purpose: Article H2s under a 2px ink rule, 3.25rem above; also the 'More in …' head after the article.

shadows.name: none
shadows.purpose: Every Tailwind shadow token resolves to none. Depth is flat paper overlap only.

shadows.name: focus-halo
shadows.purpose: Paper halo behind the 3px carbon focus outline (night counter halo in dark mode). A focus aid, not elevation.

motion.name: ease-ticket
motion.purpose: House easing for tear, stamp, chip lift and input focus.

motion.name: tear
motion.purpose: Stub tears away along the perforation while submitting. Reduced motion: no transform, opacity 0.6.

motion.name: stamp-in
motion.value: 380ms ease-ticket; from scale(1.35) rotate(-6deg) opacity 0 to scale(1) rotate(-2deg)
motion.purpose: Rubber stamp lands when a link type is recognised. Reduced motion: shown at rest.

motion.name: chip-lift
motion.purpose: Stock chips and related-tool tickets lift on hover.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Colour changes on the stub and input border.

motion.name: receipt-print
motion.value: 520ms ease-ticket; clip-path inset(0 -16px 55% -16px) + translateY(-10px) to inset(0 -16px 0 -16px)
motion.purpose: A ready or void receipt feeds out of the printer top edge first. Only under prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.

motion.name: progress-fill
motion.purpose: 5px strip in the receipt's stock along the bottom of the collect button while a file saves.

motion.name: progress-sweep
motion.value: 1100ms cubic-bezier(0.45, 0, 0.55, 1) infinite alternate; 30% strip from translateX(-30%) to 100%
motion.purpose: Indeterminate save progress. Reduced motion: the 30% strip holds still.

motion.name: skeleton-pulse
motion.purpose: Paper-tint blocks of the loading receipt. Reduced motion: static.

motion.name: fold
motion.purpose: Chevron of folded panels (receipt extras, article outline on phones).

breakpoints.name: sm
breakpoints.note: Article reading sheet insets with 6px bottom corners; blog racks go to 2 columns.

breakpoints.name: md
breakpoints.note: Root font-size steps to 106.25%. Featured article ticket puts its cover beside the paper.

breakpoints.name: lg
breakpoints.note: Hero seam: copy column + ticket column (28rem, 32rem at 1280px, 34rem from 1440px); the ticket starts on the H1 cap line and runs 2.75rem past the field, the field ends 1.5rem below the perforation, the rack's bottom sits on the perforation; results print on the counter. Blog: outline rail (11rem) + sheet (43rem), cover beside the article title. Desktop nav appears.

breakpoints.name: xl
breakpoints.note: Seam ticket 32rem, column gap 3.5rem; wide receipt preview column 15rem.

breakpoints.name: reading-wide
breakpoints.note: 84rem media query: article grid gains a sticky tool-ticket column (15rem to 18rem); the sheet column narrows to 42rem.

breakpoints.name: rc-28
breakpoints.note: Container query on a receipt: preview beside the title, tools in a row, grids 3 / dense 4.

breakpoints.name: rc-44
breakpoints.note: Container query on a receipt: grids 4 / dense 5.

breakpoints.name: rc-62
breakpoints.note: Container query on a receipt: grids 5 / dense 6.

narrative.overview:
A Pinterest link is a claim ticket and the file is what you collect at the counter. Every page is printed on a roll of ticket stock: a flat, saturated field of colour owns the top of the page, a white ticket of paper sits on it, and the primary action is the tear-off stub below a dashed perforation. Below the hero the page drops onto the counter, a cool grey ground where sections are white paper slips separated by heavy ink rules.

The world is printed, not rendered. Depth comes only from paper lying on paper; there are no drop shadows and no gradients. Corners are small and die-cut, holes are punched, perforations are dashed. Type is a condensed printing gothic (Big Shoulders Display, 800/900, uppercase) for headlines, serials, stamps and the stub, set against a plain system sans for everything a person actually reads. Each Pinterest URL type has its own stock colour, and that colour means only that URL type wherever it appears.

Honesty is part of the material: the only numerals on a ticket are real ones (the pin ID read from the pasted link, the format, the size). No invented counters.
keyCharacteristics: Full-bleed stock field behind the hero and header; counter grey below.
White ticket paper, 6px die-cut corners, punched 14px notches at the perforation.
Tear-off stub in carbon ink as the single primary action on the page.
On desktop the ticket lies across the seam: it starts on the field and its stub ends on the counter, where every result prints.
Condensed gothic uppercase for display, labels, serials, stamps; system sans for reading.
One stock colour per URL type, read from `src/lib/stocks.ts`.
Flat paper overlap only: no shadows, no gradients.

rules.name: The One Stock, One Link Rule
rules.body: A stock colour identifies exactly one Pinterest URL type, everywhere: page field, stamp, rack chip, related-tool stub. Never use a stock colour decoratively or for a different meaning.

rules.name: The Field Swap Rule
rules.body: A page sets its field with one class (`field-red`, `field-tangerine`, ...) which redefines `--field`, `--on-field`, `--on-field-2`. Components read those variables; never hard-code hero colours. A chip in the page's own stock prints on paper with a stock-coloured perforation so it does not vanish into the field.

rules.name: The Carbon Ink Rule
rules.body: On every stock except ticket red, text is carbon ink, not white.

rules.name: The Printer's Gothic Rule
rules.body: Big Shoulders is used uppercase (the serial's "No." aside) and only for display and headlines, labels, serials and numerals, stamps, and the stub and collect buttons. Never for paragraphs, inputs, or anything longer than a line or two.

rules.name: The Plain Reading Rule
rules.body: In an article the gothic only frames the text: title, section openers, labels, table heads, list numerals. Every sentence a reader reads is system sans at 1.0625rem / 1.65, no wider than 68ch, on paper.

rules.name: The Real Numerals Rule
rules.body: Gothic numerals print real values only (pin ID, step number, format, size), always with tabular figures.

rules.name: The Fixed Seam Rule
rules.body: On desktop the ticket sets the seam at first paint and nothing moves it. Whatever the form prints after a claim (loading slip, receipts, voids, history) prints on the counter below the seam, never on the field.

rules.name: The Paper Overlap Rule
rules.body: Depth is a sheet on a sheet. No drop shadows, no gradients, no blur. If something needs to stand out, change its stock or put it on paper.

rules.name: The Stub On Top Rule
rules.body: The tear-off stub is always the topmost layer of the ticket (z-index above paper; notches above both).

dos: Do print every hero on a stock field via `field-*` and read `--field` / `--on-field` in components.
Do take stock colours from `src/lib/stocks.ts`; one stock means one URL type.
Do keep depth flat: paper on field, paper on counter, stub over paper.
Do use carbon ink text on every stock except ticket red.
Do keep radii at 2 to 6px; 4px is the default for controls and slips.
Do keep the stub as the single primary action on a ticket, with 44px minimum targets elsewhere.
Do honour reduced motion: the tear becomes a fade, the stamp appears at rest.
Do print everything the form returns on desktop onto the counter below the seam: narrow results in the ticket column, wide receipts (`.rc--wide`) across both columns under the aside.
Do give every receipt the ticket's serial and a band in the stock of what was collected, and keep its one primary action in the stub's voice.
Do lay a receipt out with container queries so it reads the same in the ticket column, across the counter, or on a phone.
Do re-render the step art from `src/assets/steps/*.svg` with `node scripts/render_step_art.mjs`, keeping the WebP names and pixel sizes.
Do keep article prose in the system sans at 1.0625rem / 1.65, no wider than 68ch, on a paper sheet; the gothic frames it.
donts: Don't add drop shadows, gradients, glows or blur; the shadow tokens are `none` on purpose.
Don't use a stock colour for decoration or for a URL type it does not belong to.
Don't set paragraphs, inputs or long text in Big Shoulders.
Don't print invented counters or vanity numbers; gothic numerals carry real values only.
Don't use pill shapes or large rounded cards (rounded-full, 16px+ corners) for new surfaces.
Don't let a result, notice or loading slip move the desktop seam or print on the field above it.
Don't print a spec field whose value is not known; leave it out.
Don't edit the step WebP files by hand; change the SVG source and re-render.
